![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13934289/assets/0b47240678a326854124fe4d52398bd6db8f2dd3826713ee7449b48e4891e7cc.png)

Given the plots of $y=f(x)$ and $y=g(x)$ above, find ${h}^{′}(\frac{7}{2})$ where $h(x)=\frac{f(x)}{g(x)}.$
worked_solution:
The quotient rule for derivatives gives

$$
{h}^{′}(x)=\frac{{f}^{′}(x)\cdot g(x)-f(x)\cdot {g}^{′}(x)}{(g(x))^{2}}.
$$

As a result, we have that

$$
{h}^{′}(\frac{7}{2})=\frac{{f}^{′}(\frac{7}{2})\cdot g(\frac{7}{2})-f(\frac{7}{2})\cdot {g}^{′}(\frac{7}{2})}{{(g(\frac{7}{2}))}^{2}}
$$

From the graph above, we obtain that $f(\frac{7}{2})=g(\frac{7}{2})=1.$

Additionally:

- The slope of $f(x)$ on $x\in (3,4)$ equals $-2.$ So, ${f}^{′}(\frac{7}{2})=-2.$

- The slope of $g(x)$ on $x\in (2,4)$ equals $0.$ So, ${g}^{′}(\frac{7}{2})=0.$

Finally, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{h}^{′}(\frac{7}{2}) & =\frac{{f}^{′}(\frac{7}{2})g(\frac{7}{2})-f(\frac{7}{2}){g}^{′}(\frac{7}{2})}{{(g(\frac{7}{2}))}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{(-2)\cdot (1)-1\cdot 0}{{1}^{2}} \\  & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

EXPLANATION

The quotient rule for derivatives gives

h′(x)=f′(x)⋅g(x)−f(x)⋅g′(x)(g(x))2.

As a result, we have that

h′(72)=f′(72)⋅g(72)−f(72)⋅g′(72)(g(72))2

From the graph above, we obtain that f(72)=g(72)=1.

Additionally:

  • The slope of f(x) on x∈(3,4) equals −2. So, f′(72)=−2.

  • The slope of g(x) on x∈(2,4) equals 0. So, g′(72)=0.

Finally, we have

h′(72)=f′(72)g(72)−f(72)g′(72)(g(72))2=(−2)⋅(1)−1⋅012=−2.
